requirement:
Each public SDK item has one defining module path. The SDK exposes no public
re-exports. The chapter that introduces each supported type or free function owns its declaration.
The [public API inventory](sdk/public-api.md) links each item to that requirement,
which describes its purpose
and declares its public Rust interface, including fields, enum variants, trait
members, and inherent methods. A change to that interface requires a change to
the owning requirement. Every supported struct with public fields is
`#[non_exhaustive]`. Its constructor accepts the values needed to create it.
Additional fields have consuming builder methods that accept a concrete value.
Optional fields start as `None`. Backend inference options start empty and can
be added one key at a time.

The SDK’s public modules follow the interfaces introduced in these chapters.

- `domain`: application data and the `Domain` and `NodeContents` traits.
- `graph`: criterion definitions, graph observations, evidence, and functions for running criteria.
- `request`: `ValidationContext`, typed `Ask` builders, context values, and request phases.
- `agent`: configuration for the supplied agents.
- `sources`: project inspection, search queries, and their results.
- `outline`: selectable source contents and language rules; `outline::languages`
  supplies bundled languages, and `outline::selector` defines selector syntax.
- `storage`: filesystem evidence storage.

Source access, search engines, redaction, provider transports, agent-result paging,
and conversation machinery are implementation details of those interfaces.
rationale: Reconcile `Outline.diagnostic` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#struct[Outline]` with `requirements.sdk.public_api`. Do this in one of two ways. (1) Add a consuming builder to `impl[Outline]#1`, for example `pub fn diagnostic(mut self, diagnostic: OutlineError) -> Self`. Also declare it in the owning `requirements.sdk.outlines.Outline` interface. (2) Amend `requirements.sdk.public_api` and the owning requirement to say that `diagnostic` is a recovery output that is not settable through a builder. — `requirements.sdk.public_api` says: "Every supported struct with public fields is `#[non_exhaustive]`. Its constructor accepts the values needed to create it. Additional fields have consuming builder methods that accept a concrete value. Optional fields start as `None`." Every other root satisfies this. The configs, `SourceFile`, `TextQuery`, `StructuralQuery`, `OutlineItem`, `Segment` and the rest are `#[non_exhaustive]`, have a `new` taking the required values, and have builders for the optional fields. `option` inserts one key into an options map that starts empty. `Outline` is different. `Outline::new(items)` is its only inherent method, and `new` sets `diagnostic: None`. `diagnostic` is a public `Option<OutlineError>` field that is not a constructor argument, so it is an additional field. It has no consuming builder. Outside the crate, `#[non_exhaustive]` blocks struct-literal construction and field assignment on a value the caller builds, so there is no SDK-public way to build an `Outline` that carries a diagnostic. Only the crate-internal `Outline::from_legacy` sets it. A behavior-preserving alternative that violates the clause: leave `Outline::new` as it is and add no `diagnostic` builder. That is exactly the current code. The owning requirement `requirements.sdk.outlines.Outline` declares only `new`, so the owner and the code agree with each other but not with the public_api rule. One of the two texts has to change.

`UsageStats` exposes the following totals. `attempts` counts each request sent to the provider once. `retries` counts attempts that repeat a failed request. `failed_attempts` counts attempts that returned a provider error, including those followed by a successful retry.

`prepared_inputs` counts inputs prepared for agent messages. Each node inserted in the opening message counts once. Each requested `read_node` page and each `outgoing_edges` result counts once, including repeated reads. A requested search page counts one input per excerpt on that page. Source listings, search finalization, and opaque custom-tool results contribute zero.

`delivered_inputs` counts those inputs when the provider first responds successfully to the request carrying them. Each input counts once across retries and subsequent turns that replay the same conversation history. For example, if the opening message supplies three nodes and the provider fails permanently before replying, usage records three prepared inputs and zero delivered inputs.
Lists the selectable items from a single parse, including the root for the whole file.
`diagnostic` holds the first syntax error reported during recovery, or `None` for a clean parse.

output.rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.public_api`.

**One defining path, no public re-exports.**
- `tests/public_api.rs#fn[sdk_has_no_public_reexports]` parses every `.rs` file under `src` with tree-sitter. It fails on any `pub use` declaration.
- `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` runs `cargo doc` and compares the documented paths and item kinds to the `specified_exports` inventory. It reports both missing and unexpected items.
- That test also asserts there are no Cargo features, and it requires the shipping `habeas` consumer to compile against the SDK.
- The helper `check_hidden_exports` checks that the implementation-detail areas (source access, search engines, redaction, transports, paging) are not exposed.

**Interface declared by the owning requirement, so a change needs a requirement change.**
- `public_exports_match_the_appendix` goes through `documented_exports` into `check_declaration`. That helper compares rustdoc signatures (fields, variants, trait members, inherent methods) to the declaration in the requirement book.
- `member_order_is_free_but_field_and_method_types_are_committed` checks that `signature_parts` ignores member order. It also checks that changing a field type, a return type or a receiver mutability is detected.

**Public-field structs are `#[non_exhaustive]`.**
- `check_declaration` asserts `#[non_exhaustive]` for every published `pub struct` whose rustdoc page has `structfield` entries.

**Constructor takes the needed values, builders are consuming and take concrete values, optional fields start as `None`, options start empty and are added one key at a time.**
- `agent/config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]`:
  - `BedrockConfig::new`, `OpenAiConfig::new`, `OllamaConfig::new` and `BedrockCredentials::new` serialize to only the required fields. So the optional fields and `options` start empty or `None`.
  - Each builder is chained and sets only its own field.
  - `.option` adds keys one at a time, and a repeated key replaces the earlier value.
- `outline/selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` checks `Segment::new` (`ordinal` is `None`, and the `.ordinal` builder sets it) and `SelectorError::new`.
- `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` checks the `OutlineItem` constructor and builders. `name_span`, `header_span` and `trailer_span` start `None`, and `attachments` starts empty. It also checks `Outline::new` (`diagnostic` is `None`).
- `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[source_bytes_error_kinds_and_language_names_round_trip]` checks `SourceFile::new` (`language` is `None`, and the `.language` builder sets it).
- `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` checks `TextQuery::new` (`limit` is `None`, `context_lines` is 0, and the builders set them).
- `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` checks `StructuralQuery::new` (`limit` is `None`, and the builders set it).
- The remaining public-field structs (`Fingerprint`, `Snapshot`, `Record`, `Span`, `OutlineData`, `OutlineError`, `SearchResults`, `TextMatch`, `StructuralMatch`, the usage counters) have constructors that take all the values. They have no optional or additional fields needing builders, so I treated their constructors as pass-through. Their signatures are also pinned by the rustdoc comparison. I found no gap there.

**Public modules follow the chapters.** The `documented_exports` comparison against the inventory covers the module-to-item mapping.

I found no unchecked obligation and no weak assertion.
